To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the caregivers' knowledge of cancer care was low, their perceptions of preparedness were low, their use of coping strategies was high, and that the caregivers who used more active coping strategies had more knowledge of cancer care.
family caregivers of elderly individuals with cancer need information about the disease and care, but are not always able to get this information.
spousal caregivers of cancer patients are generally knowledgeable about cancer care, but are often unprepared for the demands of caregiving.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of cancer care on elderly spousal caregivers and the knowledge they possess regarding cancer care.
the impact of cancer on the family, and more specifically, the impact on the family caregiver.
understanding how the family caregivers of cancer patients cope with the demands of caregiving.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the family caregiver's knowledge of cancer care and perceptions of preparedness can affect the caregiver's coping strategies and, in turn, affect the caregiver's ability to cope with the cancer diagnosis.
nurses must assess the knowledge, skills, preparedness, and needs of the family caregiver in order to provide the best possible care for the patient.

nurses need to be aware of the potential stressors for caregivers, and they need to be prepared to assist family caregivers in their efforts to cope with the demands of caregiving for an elderly person with cancer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
family caregivers are not prepared to assume their roles.
nurses need to be aware of the stress that family caregivers experience when a family member is diagnosed with cancer.
the family caregivers in our sample are not well-prepared to provide care for their loved one, and that their knowledge of the disease is inadequate.
The main takeaway from our work is that
nurses must assess potential caregivers’ knowledge, skills, preparedness, and support systems in order to assist the caregiver in assuming their role.
nurses must assess potential caregivers for their knowledge, skills, coping, and preparedness.
